Item 2. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Overview. We develop, own and operate utility-scale solar generation and battery storage projects in the United States. As of June 30, 2024, we had 1,240 megawatts (MW) of solar generation and 610 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery storage in commercial operation, compared with 960 MW and 280 MWh as of June 30, 2023. Our contracted pipeline of projects under signed power purchase agreements totaled approximately 3.1 gigawatts as of June 30, 2024.

Results of Operations. Total revenues increased 37.2% to $186.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2024, compared with $135.9 million for the same period of 2023, primarily due to six solar projects and two storage projects that reached commercial operation since June 30, 2023. Operating income increased to $48.2 million from $29.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, was $121.3 million for the quarter compared with $88.0 million a year earlier.

Liquidity and Capital Resources. As of June 30, 2024, we had $412.5 million of unrestricted cash and $650.0 million of availability under our corporate revolving credit facility. We expect to invest approximately $1.4 billion in project construction during the remainder of 2024, funded by project debt, tax equity and the sale of investment tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act.

Item 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

We are exposed to changes in interest rates on our variable-rate project debt. We use interest rate swaps to hedge approximately 85% of our variable-rate project debt, converting it to fixed rates. A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in interest rates would increase our annual interest expense on the unhedged portion by approximately $2.4 million.

Item 4. Controls and Procedures

Our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of June 30, 2024. There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended June 30, 2024 that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.

PART II. OTHER INFORMATION

Item 1. Legal Proceedings

We are not currently party to any legal proceeding that we believe would have a material adverse effect on our business or financial condition.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Except as set forth below, there have been no material changes to the risk factors disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2023. In May 2024, the United States increased tariffs on lithium-ion battery cells imported from certain countries. Approximately 60% of the battery cells for our 2025 storage projects are sourced from affected countries, and the tariffs could increase our storage project costs by up to $95 million unless we qualify alternative suppliers.
